The p.Arg345Glufs*64 study found reduced neuromast FM1-43 uptake and altered tap-startle behavior compared with controls; an artificial p.Arg345* comparator also reduced dye uptake, while the extension produced a larger behavioral disturbance. Long Homer scaffolds form tetramers through their coiled-coil region. Later crystallography of Homer1/Homer3 revised the earlier parallel-tetramer model to two parallel dimers arranged tail-to-tail. nodes.description: At the tested common RNA concentration, both variant constructs reduced neuromast FM1-43 uptake without significant changes in hair-cell count or otic area. The extension caused altered tap-startle latency and distance; visual-motor responses were preserved. Cardiac abnormalities occurred at three days in the variant groups. These comparisons were between constructs at a common dose, not a dose-response experiment. The artificial stop allele is a comparator, not an established DFNA68 allele.

The 2015 study injected human p.Arg185Pro or wild-type HOMER2 mRNA into wild-type embryos. Mutant expression reduced otic-vesicle size and kinocilium number at three days; shorter kinocilia were noted qualitatively but required confirmation. Splice-blocking morpholinos did not alter the tested ear morphology. These results support a harmful mutant effect in the assay, without directly demonstrating interference with normal HOMER2 or measuring mature auditory thresholds.
nodes.id: Zebrafish HOMER2 missense mRNA overexpression model

nodes.description: At five days, morphologically normal selected larvae carrying mutant mRNA had fewer acoustic-startle responders to 70-dB, 400-Hz stimuli, while visual-motor responses were unchanged. Ear size and injected RNA abundance at three days were not significantly different. This experiment did not measure FM1-43 uptake.
nodes.id: Zebrafish HOMER2 nonstop mRNA overexpression model
